newsitem.title: CROATIA: Pliva, Zagrebacka boost sleepy Croatian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Pliva, Zagrebacka boost sleepy Croatian bourse.

text.p: Deals in drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka boosted trade on Tuesday morning as Croatian stocks drifted into Christmas slumber, market participants said.
Pliva traded at 13,700-14,000 kuna by noon after its 1/50 GDRs closed Monday at a record high of $54 each on the London Stock Exchange. It ended last week at 13,600 kuna in Zagreb.
By noon Zagrebacka ordinary shares rose to 1,050/80 kuna as its GDRs, issued at 10 to a share, also recovered to $20.56 on Seaq International.
Some traders said it was a first signal of a more general recovery which might follow in the New Year as fully-listed issues encourage investors into other stocks as well.
Others put it down to buyers being alert to the chance of a windfall by cashing in on an unexpected London increase.
"There is always some 30-50 kuna difference in Zagrebacka and 100 kuna in Pliva (between Zagreb and London prices). A strong investor can make a pretty penny on this," said one trader.
Food processor Podravka with its price around 210 kuna also attracted some buying interest but there were few other transactions.
